name: Carbon MRV
definition: Carbon MRV focuses specifically on quantifying greenhouse gas reductions or removals for carbon crediting, inventories, and results-based climate finance.
challenges: Baseline selection and methodology disputes can lead to inconsistent or inflated claims, undermining market trust. Data pipelines are fragmented, and verifiers face limited visibility into provenance—especially when data is manually collected or comes from many subcontractors. Scaling credible verification without exploding costs is a persistent bottleneck for markets and programs.
opportunities: Ethereum can anchor dataset commitments, verifier attestations, and methodology versions so later reviewers can reproduce or challenge claims with a clear integrity trail. A structured, tamper-evident record of what was measured, who verified it, and under what rules supports audit-grade provenance. Where carbon finance disburses funds, smart contracts can tie payments to verified milestones while keeping raw monitoring data offchain.
